steps.message:
ModelGate is the static scanner our model registry runs on every uploaded artifact before accepting it. It lives in `/app/modelgate/` and the registry invokes it once per artifact as `python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output /tmp/report.json /path/to/artifact`, reading the JSON report described in `/app/docs/report-schema.md`. The red team has shown that artifacts which run code when loaded get past it, and that it also flags some legitimate models. Harden the scanner so that its verdict matches the registry policy in `/app/docs/threat-model.md` for every artifact that policy covers: an artifact is `malicious` when loading it with its format's standard loader, or invoking a function it exports, would execute attacker-controlled code, start a process, access files outside the artifact, or open a network connection, and `clean` otherwise. A missed malicious artifact and a flagged legitimate one are equally wrong.

The registry grades the scanner on its own held-out corpus, built to the threat model, not on the examples in `/app/samples/`. Those examples, their labels in `/app/samples/labels.json` and the harness `/app/evaluate.py` show the formats, containers and report format, but they do not cover every technique the threat model describes. Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed, so everything the scanner needs must live there, and the command line and report schema above must keep working unchanged. Scanning must never cause any behaviour of an artifact to run: the registry runs the scanner in an isolated sandbox and treats any process it starts, any network connection it opens and any file it writes other than its report as a failed scan. The registry scans its held-out corpus of roughly 300 artifacts in one pass, invoking the scanner once per artifact; the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take more than 60 seconds, using only the Python packages already installed in this environment.

You have 28800 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.
I'll start by exploring the scanner, docs, samples, and evaluation harness to understand the current state before hardening anything.

# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious

This is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the
only definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it
but do not enumerate it.

## 1. Policy

An artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's
standard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of
the following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:

- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or
  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that
  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a
  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another
  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what
  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

Capabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a
dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached
through a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a
`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the
first `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a
finding.

Standard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:

| Format | Loader |
|---|---|
| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |
| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |
| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |
| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |
| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |

## 2. Formats and containers in scope

| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |
| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |
| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | the object pickle is the fourth stream |
| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |
| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |
| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |
| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |

Out of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,
TorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,
Keras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual
datasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.

## 3. Pickle semantics the policy follows

These are the facts of CPython's unpickler; the policy is defined in terms of
what the loader would actually do.

- `REDUCE` calls the callable with the arguments; on a class that runs
  `__new__` and `__init__`. `INST` and `OBJ` with arguments construct fully.
  `BUILD` calls `__setstate__` on the object (for `functools.partial` that
  retargets the partial). These are the ways a capability executes.
- `NEWOBJ` and `NEWOBJ_EX`, and argument-less `INST`/`OBJ`, call `__new__`
  only; they execute no capability. `PERSID`/`BINPERSID` are resolved by the
  loader's own storage mechanism and execute nothing. Importing a module
  executes no capability.
- A global that is only stored as data (placed in a container, bound as an
  attribute, memoised and never called) is not a finding, whatever its name.
  A global becomes a finding when the capability it carries is executed, no
  matter how it reached the executing opcode: directly, through the memo
  (`GET`, `BINGET`, `LONG_BINGET`), through `builtins.getattr`,
  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller`, `functools.partial`,
  `builtins.__import__` or `importlib.import_module`, or in a later stream of
  the same file.
- Module aliases are the same module: `posix` and `nt` are `os`, `_pickle` is
  `pickle`, `_io` is `io`, and every Python 2 name the unpickler maps back
  with `fix_imports` (the `_compat_pickle` tables): `__builtin__` is
  `builtins`, `copy_reg` is `copyreg`, `commands` is `subprocess`, `urllib2`
  is `urllib.request`, `httplib` is `http.client`, and so on. Pickles written
  below protocol 3 carry those Python 2 names.

Representative capability-bearing callables (a seed list, not the policy;
anything with the same capability counts):

- (A) `builtins.eval`, `builtins.exec`, `builtins.compile`, `marshal.loads`
  with `types.FunctionType`,
  `runpy.run_path`, `runpy._run_code`, `timeit.timeit`,
  `code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource`, `bdb.Bdb.run`, `pdb.run`,
  `numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring`, `logging.config.dictConfig`;
  nested loaders `pickle.loads`, `_pickle.loads`, `torch.load`,
  `torch.storage._load_from_bytes`, `numpy.load`,
  `numpy.lib.format.read_array`, `joblib.load`, `pandas.read_pickle`.
  `builtins.__import__`, `importlib.import_module`, `builtins.getattr`,
  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller` and `functools.partial`
  carry no capability of their own; they are the ways a capability-bearing
  callable is reached, and the call that reaches it is the finding.
- (B) `os.system`, `os.popen`, `os.execv`, `os.execvp`, `os.execve`,
  `os.spawnl`, `os.spawnv`, `os.posix_spawn`, `subprocess.Popen`,
  `subprocess.call`, `subprocess.run`, `subprocess.check_call`,
  `subprocess.check_output`, `pty.spawn`, `platform.popen`, `pydoc.pipepager`.
- (C) `builtins.open`, `io.open`, `os.remove`, `os.unlink`, `os.rename`,
  `os.replace`, `os.mkdir`, `os.makedirs`, `os.rmdir`, `shutil.copy`,
  `shutil.copyfile`, `shutil.move`, `shutil.rmtree`, `pathlib.Path.write_text`,
  `pathlib.Path.write_bytes`, `pathlib.Path.unlink`; a nested loader given a
  path instead of embedded data reads that path.
- (D) `socket.create_connection`, `socket.socket.connect`,
  `urllib.request.urlopen`, `http.client.HTTPConnection.connect` and
  `.request`, `ftplib.FTP.connect` and `ftplib.FTP(host)`,
  `smtplib.SMTP(host)`, `ssl.get_server_certificate`, `webbrowser.open`. The
  capability is in the call that connects: constructing a client object
  without a host (`socket.socket()`, `http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)`,
  `ftplib.FTP()`, `xmlrpc.client.ServerProxy(uri)`) opens nothing.

## 4. TensorFlow op table (closed)

For TensorFlow graphs the table is the policy: an op listed here has the
capability listed, and an op not listed has none, wherever it appears.

| Capability | Ops |
|---|---|
| (A) code execution | `PyFunc` `PyFuncStateless` `EagerPyFunc` |
| (C) file access | `ReadFile` `WriteFile` `MatchingFiles` `MatchingFilesDataset` `ImmutableConst` `WholeFileReader` `WholeFileReaderV2` `TextLineReader` `TextLineReaderV2` `FixedLengthRecordReader` `FixedLengthRecordReaderV2` `TFRecordReader` `TFRecordReaderV2` `LMDBReader` `LMDBDataset` `ExperimentalLMDBDataset` `TextLineDataset` `TFRecordDataset` `FixedLengthRecordDataset` `DatasetToTFRecord` `ExperimentalDatasetToTFRecord` `SaveDataset` `SaveDatasetV2` `LoadDataset` `SnapshotDataset` `SnapshotDatasetV2` `LoadAndRemapMatrix` `GenerateVocabRemapping` `Save` `SaveSlices` `Restore` `RestoreSlice` |
| (D) network | `DataServiceDataset` `DataServiceDatasetV2` `DataServiceDatasetV3` `DataServiceDatasetV4` `RegisterDataset` `RegisterDatasetV2` `DistributedSave` |
| never a finding | `SaveV2` `RestoreV2` `MergeV2Checkpoints` `ShardedFilename` `ShardedFilespec` (the standard checkpoint saver that every real SavedModel carries), and every op not listed above |

Op names are exact and case-sensitive. Node names, device strings, attribute
values and tensor contents carry no capability.

## 5. Keras

A `Lambda` layer whose `function` carries serialized bytecode is (A):
`"function": {"class_name": "__lambda__", "config": {"code": "<base64>", "defaults": ..., "closure": ...}}`. A `Lambda` whose function is a named
function reference (`{"module": "builtins", "class_name": "function",
"config": "relu", ...}`), an `Activation` layer, and every other layer type are
clean. Layers are found wherever the JSON nests them: `layers`, the `layer` of
a wrapper, and the `config` of a nested model.

## 1. Policy

An artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's
standard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of
the following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:

- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or
  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that
  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a
  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another
  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what
  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

Capabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a
dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached
through a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a
`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the
first `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a
finding.

Standard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:

| Format | Loader |
|---|---|
| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |
| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |
| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |

| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |

  with `fix_imports` (the `_compat_pickle` tables): `__builtin__` is
  `builtins`, `copy_reg` is `copyreg`, `commands` is `subprocess`, `urllib2`
  is `urllib.request`, `httplib` is `http.client`, and so on. Pickles written
  below protocol 3 carry those Python 2 names.

Representative capability-bearing callables (a seed list, not the policy;
anything with the same capability counts):

- (A) `builtins.eval`, `builtins.exec`, `builtins.compile`, `marshal.loads`
  with `types.FunctionType`,
  `runpy.run_path`, `runpy._run_code`, `timeit.timeit`,
  `code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource`, `bdb.Bdb.run`, `pdb.run`,
  `numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring`, `logging.config.dictConfig`;
  nested loaders `pickle.loads`, `_pickle.loads`, `torch.load`,
  `torch.storage._load_from_bytes`, `numpy.load`,
  `numpy.lib.format.read_array`, `joblib.load`, `pandas.read_pickle`.
  `builtins.__import__`, `importlib.import_module`, `builtins.getattr`,
  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller` and `functools.partial`
  carry no capability of their own; they are the ways a capability-bearing
  callable is reached, and the call that reaches it is the finding.
- (B) `os.system`, `os.popen`, `os.execv`, `os.execvp`, `os.execve`,
  `os.spawnl`, `os.spawnv`, `os.posix_spawn`, `subprocess.Popen`,
  `subprocess.call`, `subprocess.run`, `subprocess.check_call`,
  `subprocess.check_output`, `pty.spawn`, `platform.popen`, `pydoc.pipepager`.
- (C) `builtins.open`, `io.open`, `os.remove`, `os.unlink`, `os.rename`,
  `os.replace`, `os.mkdir`, `os.makedirs`, `os.rmdir`, `shutil.copy`,
  `shutil.copyfile`, `shutil.move`, `shutil.rmtree`, `pathlib.Path.write_text`,
  `pathlib.Path.write_bytes`, `pathlib.Path.unlink`; a nested loader given a
  path instead of embedded data reads that path.
- (D) `socket.create_connection`, `socket.socket.connect`,
  `urllib.request.urlopen`, `http.client.HTTPConnection.connect` and
  `.request`, `ftplib.FTP.connect` and `ftplib.FTP(host)`,
  `smtplib.SMTP(host)`, `ssl.get_server_certificate`, `webbrowser.open`. The
  capability is in the call that connects: constructing a client object
  without a host (`socket.socket()`, `http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)`,
  `ftplib.FTP()`, `xmlrpc.client.ServerProxy(uri)`) opens nothing.

## 4. TensorFlow op table (closed)

For TensorFlow graphs the table is the policy: an op listed here has the
capability listed, and an op not listed has none, wherever it appears.

| Capability | Ops |
|---|---|
| (A) code execution | `PyFunc` `PyFuncStateless` `EagerPyFunc` |
| (C) file access | `ReadFile` `WriteFile` `MatchingFiles` `MatchingFilesDataset` `ImmutableConst` `WholeFileReader` `WholeFileReaderV2` `TextLineReader` `TextLineReaderV2` `FixedLengthRecordReader` `FixedLengthRecordReaderV2` `TFRecordReader` `TFRecordReaderV2` `LMDBReader` `LMDBDataset` `ExperimentalLMDBDataset` `TextLineDataset` `TFRecordDataset` `FixedLengthRecordDataset` `DatasetToTFRecord` `ExperimentalDatasetToTFRecord` `SaveDataset` `SaveDatasetV2` `LoadDataset` `SnapshotDataset` `SnapshotDatasetV2` `LoadAndRemapMatrix` `GenerateVocabRemapping` `Save` `SaveSlices` `Restore` `RestoreSlice` |

values and tensor contents carry no capability.

## 5. Keras

A `Lambda` layer whose `function` carries serialized bytecode is (A):
`"function": {"class_name": "__lambda__", "config": {"code": "<base64>", "defaults": ..., "closure": ...}}`. A `Lambda` whose function is a named

# ModelGate scanner contract

## Invocation

The registry runs the scanner once per uploaded artifact, from a working
directory that is not `/app`, with no environment variables beyond `PATH`,
`HOME` and `TMPDIR`:

```
python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path>
```

`<path>` is the artifact: a file, or a directory for a TensorFlow SavedModel.
The scanner must write exactly one JSON document to `<report.json>` and exit
with status 0 once it is written. Exit status 2 is reserved for a usage error
(missing or unknown arguments). Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed to the
registry; the scanner may use nothing outside it except the Python packages
already installed in this environment. The registry's held-out corpus holds
roughly 300 artifacts and is scanned in one pass, one invocation per artifact:
the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take
more than 60 seconds.

## Report

```json
{
  "scanner": "modelgate",
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "<the path argument exactly as given>",
      "verdict": "malicious",
      "findings": [
        {
          "kind": "code-execution",
          "location": "archive/data.pkl",
          "detail": "REDUCE builtins.eval"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- `results` has exactly one entry per path argument, in argument order, and
  `path` repeats the argument byte for byte.
- `verdict` is `"malicious"` or `"clean"`.
- `findings` is a list that is non-empty if and only if the verdict is
  `"malicious"`.
- each finding is an object with exactly the three string keys `kind`,
  `location` and `detail`.
- `kind` is one of `"code-execution"`, `"process"`, `"file-access"`,
  `"network"`, `"unsupported"`.
- `location` names where the finding is (a container member, a pickle stream
  and opcode offset, a graph node, a layer path) and `detail` says what it is.
  Both are free text for humans.

An artifact the scanner cannot analyse must still receive a verdict. The
registry policy is fail-closed: report it `"malicious"` with one finding of
kind `"unsupported"` that says why.

A report that is missing, is not valid JSON, violates any rule above, or is
not written within the time limit counts as a wrong verdict for that artifact.
=== evaluate.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the ModelGate scanner over /app/samples the way the registry does and
compare its verdicts with /app/samples/labels.json.

Usage: python3 /app/evaluate.py [--samples DIR] [--scanner /app/modelgate/cli.py]

The scanner is invoked as a separate process per artifact, with the same
command line the registry uses, so this script never imports the scanner.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

KINDS = {"code-execution", "process", "file-access", "network", "unsupported"}


def run_scanner(cli, artifact, timeout=60):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        report = os.path.join(tmp, "report.json")
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-I", cli, "scan", "--output", report, artifact]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, "timeout", time.monotonic() - started
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"exit {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr.strip()[-200:]}", seconds
        try:
            with open(report, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                doc = json.load(f)
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            return None, f"unreadable report: {exc}", seconds
        return doc, None, seconds


def check_schema(doc, artifact):
    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or doc.get("scanner") != "modelgate":
        return "top-level object with scanner == modelgate expected"
    results = doc.get("results")
    if not isinstance(results, list) or len(results) != 1:
        return "results must hold exactly one entry"
    entry = results[0]
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"path", "verdict", "findings"}:
        return "entry must have exactly path, verdict, findings"
    if entry["path"] != artifact:
        return "path must repeat the argument exactly"
    if entry["verdict"] not in ("malicious", "clean"):
        return "verdict must be malicious or clean"
    findings = entry["findings"]
    if not isinstance(findings, list):
        return "findings must be a list"
    if (entry["verdict"] == "malicious") != (len(findings) > 0):
        return "findings must be non-empty iff verdict is malicious"
    for finding in findings:
        if not isinstance(finding, dict) or set(finding) != {"kind", "location", "detail"}:
            return "each finding needs exactly kind, location, detail"
        if not all(isinstance(finding[k], str) for k in ("kind", "location", "detail")):
            return "finding fields must be strings"
        if finding["kind"] not in KINDS:
            return f"unknown finding kind {finding['kind']!r}"
    return None


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--samples", default="/app/samples")
    parser.add_argument("--scanner", default="/app/modelgate/cli.py")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(os.path.join(args.samples, "labels.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        labels = json.load(f)

    rows = []
    for name in sorted(labels):
        expected = labels[name]
        artifact = os.path.join(args.samples, name)
        doc, error, seconds = run_scanner(args.scanner, artifact)
        if error is None:
            error = check_schema(doc, artifact)
        if error is None:
            entry = doc["results"][0]
            verdict = entry["verdict"]
            kinds = sorted({f["kind"] for f in entry["findings"]})
        else:
            verdict = "invalid"
            kinds = []
        rows.append((name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds))

    width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
    print(f"{'artifact':<{width}}  expected   reported   ok  seconds  findings")
    for name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds in rows:
        ok = "yes" if verdict == expected else "NO"
        extra = ",".join(kinds) if error is None else f"ERROR: {error}"
        print(f"{name:<{width}}  {expected:<9}  {verdict:<9}  {ok:<3} {seconds:7.2f}  {extra}")

    malicious = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "malicious"]
    clean = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "clean"]
    caught = sum(1 for r in malicious if r[2] == "malicious")
    false_pos = sum(1 for r in clean if r[2] != "clean")
    invalid = sum(1 for r in rows if r[4] is not None)
    print()
    print(f"recall: {caught}/{len(malicious)} malicious artifacts reported malicious")
    print(f"false positives: {false_pos}/{len(clean)} clean artifacts not reported clean")
    print(f"invalid reports: {invalid}")
    print(f"slowest scan: {max(r[5] for r in rows):.2f} s")
    return 0 if caught == len(malicious) and false_pos == 0 and invalid == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    if not isinstance(results, list) or len(results) != 1:
        return "results must hold exactly one entry"
    entry = results[0]
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"path", "verdict", "findings"}:
        return "entry must have exactly path, verdict, findings"
    if entry["path"] != artifact:
        return "path must repeat the argument exactly"
    if entry["verdict"] not in ("malicious", "clean"):
        return "verdict must be malicious or clean"
    findings = entry["findings"]
    if not isinstance(findings, list):
        return "findings must be a list"
    if (entry["verdict"] == "malicious") != (len(findings) > 0):
        return "findings must be non-empty iff verdict is malicious"
    for finding in findings:
        if not isinstance(finding, dict) or set(finding) != {"kind", "location", "detail"}:
            return "each finding needs exactly kind, location, detail"
        if not all(isinstance(finding[k], str) for k in ("kind", "location", "detail")):
            return "finding fields must be strings"
        if finding["kind"] not in KINDS:
            return f"unknown finding kind {finding['kind']!r}"
    return None


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--samples", default="/app/samples")
    parser.add_argument("--scanner", default="/app/modelgate/cli.py")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(os.path.join(args.samples, "labels.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        labels = json.load(f)

    rows = []
    for name in sorted(labels):
        expected = labels[name]
        artifact = os.path.join(args.samples, name)
        doc, error, seconds = run_scanner(args.scanner, artifact)
        if error is None:
            error = check_schema(doc, artifact)
        if error is None:
            entry = doc["results"][0]
            verdict = entry["verdict"]
            kinds = sorted({f["kind"] for f in entry["findings"]})
        else:
            verdict = "invalid"
            kinds = []
        rows.append((name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds))

    width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
    print(f"{'artifact':<{width}}  expected   reported   ok  seconds  findings")
    for name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds in rows:
        ok = "yes" if verdict == expected else "NO"
        extra = ",".join(kinds) if error is None else f"ERROR: {error}"
        print(f"{name:<{width}}  {expected:<9}  {verdict:<9}  {ok:<3} {seconds:7.2f}  {extra}")

    malicious = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "malicious"]
    clean = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "clean"]
    caught = sum(1 for r in malicious if r[2] == "malicious")
    false_pos = sum(1 for r in clean if r[2] != "clean")
    invalid = sum(1 for r in rows if r[4] is not None)
    print()
    print(f"recall: {caught}/{len(malicious)} malicious artifacts reported malicious")
    print(f"false positives: {false_pos}/{len(clean)} clean artifacts not reported clean")
    print(f"invalid reports: {invalid}")
    print(f"slowest scan: {max(r[5] for r in rows):.2f} s")
    return 0 if caught == len(malicious) and false_pos == 0 and invalid == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# ModelGate scanner contract

## Invocation

The registry runs the scanner once per uploaded artifact, from a working
directory that is not `/app`, with no environment variables beyond `PATH`,
`HOME` and `TMPDIR`:

```
python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path>
```

`<path>` is the artifact: a file, or a directory for a TensorFlow SavedModel.
The scanner must write exactly one JSON document to `<report.json>` and exit
with status 0 once it is written. Exit status 2 is reserved for a usage error
(missing or unknown arguments). Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed to the
registry; the scanner may use nothing outside it except the Python packages
already installed in this environment. The registry's held-out corpus holds
roughly 300 artifacts and is scanned in one pass, one invocation per artifact:
the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take
more than 60 seconds.

## Report

```json
{
  "scanner": "modelgate",
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "<the path argument exactly as given>",
      "verdict": "malicious",
      "findings": [
        {
          "kind": "code-execution",
          "location": "archive/data.pkl",
          "detail": "REDUCE builtins.eval"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- `results` has exactly one entry per path argument, in argument order, and
  `path` repeats the argument byte for byte.
- `verdict` is `"malicious"` or `"clean"`.
- `findings` is a list that is non-empty if and only if the verdict is
  `"malicious"`.
- each finding is an object with exactly the three string keys `kind`,
  `location` and `detail`.
- `kind` is one of `"code-execution"`, `"process"`, `"file-access"`,
  `"network"`, `"unsupported"`.
- `location` names where the finding is (a container member, a pickle stream
  and opcode offset, a graph node, a layer path) and `detail` says what it is.
  Both are free text for humans.

An artifact the scanner cannot analyse must still receive a verdict. The
registry policy is fail-closed: report it `"malicious"` with one finding of
kind `"unsupported"` that says why.

A report that is missing, is not valid JSON, violates any rule above, or is
not written within the time limit counts as a wrong verdict for that artifact.
=== evaluate.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the ModelGate scanner over /app/samples the way the registry does and
compare its verdicts with /app/samples/labels.json.

Usage: python3 /app/evaluate.py [--samples DIR] [--scanner /app/modelgate/cli.py]

The scanner is invoked as a separate process per artifact, with the same
command line the registry uses, so this script never imports the scanner.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

KINDS = {"code-execution", "process", "file-access", "network", "unsupported"}


def run_scanner(cli, artifact, timeout=60):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        report = os.path.join(tmp, "report.json")
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-I", cli, "scan", "--output", report, artifact]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, "timeout", time.monotonic() - started
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"exit {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr.strip()[-200:]}", seconds
        try:
            with open(report, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                doc = json.load(f)
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            return None, f"unreadable report: {exc}", seconds
        return doc, None, seconds

        return "top-level object with scanner == modelgate expected"

        return "path must repeat the argument exactly"
    if entry["verdict"] not in ("malicious", "clean"):
        return "verdict must be malicious or clean"
    findings = entry["findings"]
    if not isinstance(findings, list):
        return "findings must be a list"
    if (entry["verdict"] == "malicious") != (len(findings) > 0):
        return "findings must be non-empty iff verdict is malicious"
    for finding in findings:
        if not isinstance(finding, dict) or set(finding) != {"kind", "location", "detail"}:
            return "each finding needs exactly kind, location, detail"
        if not all(isinstance(finding[k], str) for k in ("kind", "location", "detail")):
            return "finding fields must be strings"
        if finding["kind"] not in KINDS:
            return f"unknown finding kind {finding['kind']!r}"
    return None


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--samples", default="/app/samples")
    parser.add_argument("--scanner", default="/app/modelgate/cli.py")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(os.path.join(args.samples, "labels.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        labels = json.load(f)

    rows = []
    for name in sorted(labels):
        expected = labels[name]
        artifact = os.path.join(args.samples, name)
        doc, error, seconds = run_scanner(args.scanner, artifact)
        if error is None:
            error = check_schema(doc, artifact)
        if error is None:
            entry = doc["results"][0]
            verdict = entry["verdict"]
            kinds = sorted({f["kind"] for f in entry["findings"]})
        else:
            verdict = "invalid"
            kinds = []
        rows.append((name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds))

    width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
    print(f"{'artifact':<{width}}  expected   reported   ok  seconds  findings")
    for name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds in rows:
        ok = "yes" if verdict == expected else "NO"
        extra = ",".join(kinds) if error is None else f"ERROR: {error}"
        print(f"{name:<{width}}  {expected:<9}  {verdict:<9}  {ok:<3} {seconds:7.2f}  {extra}")

    malicious = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "malicious"]
    clean = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "clean"]
    caught = sum(1 for r in malicious if r[2] == "malicious")
    false_pos = sum(1 for r in clean if r[2] != "clean")
    invalid = sum(1 for r in rows if r[4] is not None)
    print()
    print(f"recall: {caught}/{len(malicious)} malicious artifacts reported malicious")
    print(f"false positives: {false_pos}/{len(clean)} clean artifacts not reported clean")
    print(f"invalid reports: {invalid}")
    print(f"slowest scan: {max(r[5] for r in rows):.2f} s")
    return 0 if caught == len(malicious) and false_pos == 0 and invalid == 0 else 1

arguments.content:
"""What the scanner looks for, expressed as capabilities rather than names.

The registry policy (``/app/docs/threat-model.md``) defines an artifact as
malicious when loading it, or invoking a function it exports, would execute
attacker-controlled code (A), start a process (B), touch a file outside the
artifact (C) or open a network connection (D).  The tables below name the
callables and graph ops that carry those capabilities.  A name is only a
finding when the capability is *executed*; the pickle interpreter in
``pickle_scan`` decides that, this module only says what each callable is.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import _compat_pickle

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Finding kinds (must match /app/docs/report-schema.md).
CODE = "code-execution"
PROC = "process"
FILE = "file-access"
NET = "network"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Module-alias resolution.  The unpickler treats several module names as the
# same module; a capability reached through an alias is the same capability.
# `_compat_pickle` carries the Python 2 -> 3 tables the unpickler applies with
# fix_imports; the extras below are genuine current aliases (posix/nt re-export
# os, _pickle is the C pickle, and so on) that hold at every protocol.
_EXTRA_MODULE_ALIASES = {
    "posix": "os",
    "nt": "os",
    "_pickle": "pickle",
    "cPickle": "pickle",
    "_io": "io",
    "cStringIO": "io",
    "StringIO": "io",
    "_socket": "socket",
    "_functools": "functools",
    "_operator": "operator",
    "_collections": "collections",
    "_json": "json",
}


def resolve(module: str, name: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Map (module, name) through the unpickler's alias tables."""
    key = (module, name)
    if key in _compat_pickle.NAME_MAPPING:
        module, name = _compat_pickle.NAME_MAPPING[key]
    elif module in _compat_pickle.IMPORT_MAPPING:
        module = _compat_pickle.IMPORT_MAPPING[module]
    module = _EXTRA_MODULE_ALIASES.get(module, module)
    # A dotted first component can itself be an alias (e.g. ``posix.path``).
    head, _, rest = module.partition(".")
    if rest and head in _EXTRA_MODULE_ALIASES:
        module = _EXTRA_MODULE_ALIASES[head] + "." + rest
    return module, name


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Capability table.  Keys are fully-qualified dotted names (module + qualname)
# after alias resolution.  Value is (kind, trigger):
#   "call"      -> a finding whenever the callable is invoked.
#   "call_args" -> a finding only when invoked with at least one argument
#                  (constructors that connect only when given a host, etc.).
CAPABILITIES: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}


def _add(kind, trigger, names):
    for n in names:
        CAPABILITIES[n] = (kind, trigger)


# (A) code execution ---------------------------------------------------------
_add(CODE, "call", [
    "builtins.eval", "builtins.exec", "builtins.compile", "builtins.execfile",
    "builtins.breakpoint",
    "types.FunctionType", "types.CodeType",
    "marshal.loads",
    "runpy.run_path", "runpy._run_code", "runpy._run_module_code",
    "runpy.run_module", "runpy.run_module_as_main",
    "timeit.timeit", "timeit.repeat", "timeit.Timer",
    "code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource",
    "code.InteractiveInterpreter.runcode",
    "code.InteractiveConsole.interact", "code.interact",
    "bdb.Bdb.run", "bdb.Bdb.runeval", "bdb.Bdb.runcall",
    "pdb.run", "pdb.runeval", "pdb.runcall", "pdb.Pdb.run",
    "numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring",
    "logging.config.dictConfig", "logging.config.fileConfig",
    "logging.config.listen",
    "cProfile.run", "cProfile.runctx", "profile.run", "profile.runctx",
])

# (B) process ----------------------------------------------------------------
_add(PROC, "call", [
    "os.system", "os.popen", "os.popen2", "os.popen3", "os.popen4",
    "os.posix_spawn", "os.posix_spawnp", "os.startfile",
    "os.execl", "os.execle", "os.execlp", "os.execlpe",
    "os.execv", "os.execve", "os.execvp", "os.execvpe",

"""Keras HDF5 scanning: Lambda layers in the model configuration."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

from modelgate.report import Finding


def scan_h5(path: str, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    import h5py  # lazy: only needed for Keras files

    with h5py.File(path, "r") as fh:
        raw = fh.attrs.get("model_config")
    if raw is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(raw, bytes):
        raw = raw.decode("utf-8")
    config = json.loads(raw)
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for i, layer in enumerate(config.get("config", {}).get("layers", [])):
        if layer.get("class_name") == "Lambda":
            findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}:layers[{i}]", "Lambda layer"))
    return findings

arguments.content:
"""TensorFlow SavedModel scanning.

Parse ``saved_model.pb`` (or ``saved_model.pbtxt``) statically with the
vendored protobuf bindings -- TensorFlow itself is never imported, so no graph
is ever built or run -- and check the op of every node that is in scope: for
every ``meta_graphs[*]``, the top-level ``graph_def.node`` and every
``graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`` (which is where functions reached
through ``If``/``While``/``PartitionedCall``/... node attributes live).  An op
is judged only by the closed table in ``policy.TF_OPS``; node names, device
strings, attribute values and tensor contents carry no capability.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

from modelgate.policy import TF_OPS
from modelgate.report import Finding


def _scan_nodes(nodes, where, findings):
    for node in nodes:
        kind = TF_OPS.get(node.op)
        if kind:
            findings.append(Finding(kind, f"{where}:{node.name}", f"op {node.op}"))


def _load_saved_model(path):
    from modelgate.tfproto import saved_model_pb2

    sm = saved_model_pb2.SavedModel()
    pb = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pb")
    pbtxt = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pbtxt")
    if os.path.isfile(pb):
        with open(pb, "rb") as fh:
            sm.ParseFromString(fh.read())
        return sm
    if os.path.isfile(pbtxt):
        from google.protobuf import text_format

        with open(pbtxt, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            text_format.Parse(fh.read(), sm)
        return sm
    return None


def scan_saved_model_dir(path):
    sm = _load_saved_model(path)
    if sm is None:
        return [Finding("unsupported", path, "directory has no saved_model.pb or saved_model.pbtxt")]
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for gi, mg in enumerate(sm.meta_graphs):
        graph = mg.graph_def
        _scan_nodes(graph.node, f"meta_graph[{gi}].graph_def", findings)
        for fi, func in enumerate(graph.library.function):
            name = func.signature.name or str(fi)
            _scan_nodes(func.node_def, f"meta_graph[{gi}].library.{name}", findings)
    return findings

vendored protobuf bindings -- TensorFlow itself is never imported, so no graph
is ever built or run -- and check the op of every node that is in scope: for
every ``meta_graphs[*]``, the top-level ``graph_def.node`` and every
``graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`` (which is where functions reached
through ``If``/``While``/``PartitionedCall``/... node attributes live).  An op
is judged only by the closed table in ``policy.TF_OPS``; node names, device
strings, attribute values and tensor contents carry no capability.
"""

import os

from modelgate.policy import TF_OPS
from modelgate.report import Finding


def _scan_nodes(nodes, where, findings):
    for node in nodes:
        kind = TF_OPS.get(node.op)
        if kind:
            findings.append(Finding(kind, f"{where}:{node.name}", f"op {node.op}"))

        with open(pbtxt, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            text_format.Parse(fh.read(), sm)
        return sm
    return None

    sm = _load_saved_model(path)
    if sm is None:
        return [Finding("unsupported", path, "directory has no saved_model.pb or saved_model.pbtxt")]

"""Route an artifact to the right analyser and build its result.

A directory is a TensorFlow SavedModel; everything else is a file whose format
is decided by its content (``containers.scan_bytes``), not its extension.  Any
exception raised while scanning is turned by the CLI into a fail-closed
``unsupported`` verdict, so every artifact receives a verdict.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

from modelgate import containers, savedmodel_scan
from modelgate.report import Result

_MAX_READ = 512 * 1024 * 1024


def scan_path(path: str) -> Result:
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        return Result(path, savedmodel_scan.scan_saved_model_dir(path))
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        data = fh.read(_MAX_READ)
    name = os.path.basename(path.rstrip("/")) or path
    return Result(path, containers.scan_bytes(data, name, depth=0, budget={"ops": 0}))

"""Tiny pickle opcode assembler for building adversarial test pickles WITHOUT
executing anything (we only emit bytes)."""
import struct

PROTO2 = b"\x80\x02"
MARK = b"("
STOP = b"."
REDUCE = b"R"
BUILD = b"b"
TUPLE = b"t"
TUPLE1 = b"\x85"
TUPLE2 = b"\x86"
TUPLE3 = b"\x87"
EMPTY_TUPLE = b")"
EMPTY_LIST = b"]"
EMPTY_DICT = b"}"
NONE = b"N"
APPEND = b"a"
APPENDS = b"e"
SETITEM = b"s"
SETITEMS = b"u"
STACK_GLOBAL = b"\x93"
MEMOIZE = b"\x94"
NEWOBJ = b"\x81"
OBJ = b"o"


def G(mod, name):            # GLOBAL (text form)
    return b"c" + mod.encode() + b"\n" + name.encode() + b"\n"


def I(mod, name):            # INST (text form); pops mark args
    return b"i" + mod.encode() + b"\n" + name.encode() + b"\n"


def U(s):                    # SHORT_BINUNICODE / BINUNICODE
    b = s.encode()
    if len(b) < 256:
        return b"\x8c" + bytes([len(b)]) + b
    return b"X" + struct.pack("<I", len(b)) + b


def BY(b):                   # SHORT_BINBYTES / BINBYTES
    if len(b) < 256:
        return b"C" + bytes([len(b)]) + b
    return b"B" + struct.pack("<I", len(b)) + b


def KI(n):                   # small int
    if 0 <= n < 256:
        return b"K" + bytes([n])
    return b"J" + struct.pack("<i", n)


def PUT(i):
    return b"q" + bytes([i])


def GET(i):
    return b"h" + bytes([i])


def SG(mod, name):           # STACK_GLOBAL from two unicode pushes
    return U(mod) + U(name) + STACK_GLOBAL


def wrap(body):
    return PROTO2 + body + STOP

def npy_object(payload_bytes):

def add_node(container, name, op, inputs=()):

        f.attrs["keras_version"] = "3.10.0"
        f.attrs["backend"] = "tensorflow"
    labels[name] = label

    p = os.path.join(OUT, name)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(p, "w") as zf:
        zf.writestr("config.json", json.dumps(cfg))
        zf.writestr("metadata.json", json.dumps({"keras_version": "3.10.0"}))
        zf.writestr("model.weights.h5", b"\x89HDF\r\n\x1a\n dummy weights")
    labels[name] = label

    {"class_name": "TimeDistributed", "config": {"name": "td", "layer": lambda_layer(BYTECODE_FN)}}]), "malicious")

write_h5("k_h5_nested.h5", FUNCTIONAL([
    {"class_name": "Sequential", "config": {"name": "sub", "layers": [dense(), lambda_layer(BYTECODE_FN)]}}]), "malicious")
# activation only
write_h5("k_h5_activation.h5", FUNCTIONAL([dense(),
    {"class_name": "Activation", "config": {"name": "act", "activation": "relu"}}]), "clean")
# no model_config (weights only)
p = os.path.join(OUT, "k_h5_weights.h5")
with h5py.File(p, "w") as f:
    g = f.create_group("model_weights")
    g.attrs["layer_names"] = ["d"]
labels["k_h5_weights.h5"] = "clean"

write_keras("k_keras_bytecode.keras", FUNCTIONAL([dense(), lambda_layer(BYTECODE_FN)]), "malicious")
write_keras("k_keras_named.keras", FUNCTIONAL([dense(), lambda_layer(NAMED_FN)]), "clean")
write_keras("k_keras_wrapper.keras", FUNCTIONAL([
    {"class_name": "Bidirectional", "config": {"name": "bi", "layer": lambda_layer(BYTECODE_FN)}}]), "malicious")

json.dump(labels, open(os.path.join(OUT, "labels.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print("corpus now has", len(labels), "artifacts")

    python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path> [<path> ...]

Writes one JSON report (see /app/docs/report-schema.md) and exits 0 once it
is written; exits 2 on a usage error.  ``-I`` keeps the script directory off
sys.path, so the package directory's parent is added explicitly below.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from modelgate import __version__  # noqa: E402
from modelgate import dispatch  # noqa: E402
from modelgate.report import Finding, Result, to_json  # noqa: E402


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="modelgate", description="static scanner for model artifacts")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"modelgate {__version__}")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    scan = sub.add_parser("scan", help="scan one or more artifacts")
    scan.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="where to write the JSON report")
    scan.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="artifact files, or SavedModel directories")
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        return 2 if exc.code else 0

    results = []
    for path in args.paths:
        try:
            results.append(dispatch.scan_path(path))
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash must still yield a verdict
            results.append(Result(path, [Finding("unsupported", path, f"scanner error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")]))
    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(to_json(results))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def _load_saved_model(path):
    from modelgate.tfproto import saved_model_pb2

    sm = saved_model_pb2.SavedModel()
    pb = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pb")
    pbtxt = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pbtxt")
    if os.path.isfile(pb):
        with open(pb, "rb") as fh:
            sm.ParseFromString(fh.read())
        return sm
    if os.path.isfile(pbtxt):
        from google.protobuf import text_format

        with open(pbtxt, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            text_format.Parse(fh.read(), sm)
        return sm
    return None


def scan_saved_model_dir(path):
    sm = _load_saved_model(path)
    if sm is None:
        return [Finding("unsupported", path, "directory has no saved_model.pb or saved_model.pbtxt")]
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for gi, mg in enumerate(sm.meta_graphs):
        graph = mg.graph_def
        _scan_nodes(graph.node, f"meta_graph[{gi}].graph_def", findings)
        for fi, func in enumerate(graph.library.function):
            name = func.signature.name or str(fi)
            _scan_nodes(func.node_def, f"meta_graph[{gi}].library.{name}", findings)
    return findings

vendored protobuf bindings -- TensorFlow itself is never imported, so no graph
is ever built or run -- and check the op of every node that is in scope: for
every ``meta_graphs[*]``, the top-level ``graph_def.node`` and every
``graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`` (which is where functions reached
through ``If``/``While``/``PartitionedCall``/... node attributes live).  An op
is judged only by the closed table in ``policy.TF_OPS``; node names, device
strings, attribute values and tensor contents carry no capability.

from modelgate.report import Finding


def _scan_nodes(nodes, where, findings):

        kind = TF_OPS.get(node.op)

            findings.append(Finding(kind, f"{where}:{node.name}", f"op {node.op}"))

        return sm
    return None

    def run(self, gen, base):
        """Drive the opcode generator, rebasing offsets onto ``base``.  Returns
        the STOP offset (relative to base) or None.  Consumes lazily and stops
        at the op budget so a huge pickle is never fully materialised."""
        for op, arg, off in gen:
            self.budget["ops"] += 1
            if self.budget["ops"] > _MAX_OPS:
                return None
            name = op.name
            if name == "STOP":
                return off
            handler = _HANDLERS.get(name)
            if handler is not None:
                handler(self, arg, base + off)
            # opcodes without a handler have no effect we care about
        return None

   522	def scan_pickle(data, location, depth=0, budget=None):
   523	    """Scan one file that is a sequence of one or more concatenated pickles.
   524	
   525	    Every stream is analysed (a payload may hide in the second stream, as the
   526	    policy notes); trailing non-pickle bytes -- the raw storages of a legacy
   527	    torch checkpoint -- end the walk once at least one stream has parsed.
   528	    """
   529	    if budget is None:
   530	        budget = {"ops": 0}
   531	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   532	    pos = 0
   533	    stream = 0
   534	    n = len(data)
   535	    parsed_any = False
   536	    while pos < n and budget["ops"] <= _MAX_OPS:
   537	        stream += 1
   538	        machine = _Machine(data, location, stream, findings, depth, budget)
   539	        try:
   540	            stop_off = machine.run(pickletools.genops(data[pos:]), pos)
   541	        except Exception:
   542	            # A stream that will not parse: trailing raw bytes after an earlier
   543	            # pickle (a legacy torch checkpoint's storages) end the walk; a
   544	            # first stream that will not parse at all is fail-closed.
   545	            if parsed_any or findings:
   546	                break
   547	            return [Finding("unsupported", location, "could not parse pickle opcodes")]
   548	        parsed_any = True
   549	        if stop_off is None:
   550	            break                   # no STOP: truncated tail or op budget hit
   551	        pos += stop_off + 1
   552	    if not parsed_any:
   553	        return [Finding("unsupported", location, "empty pickle")]
   554	    return findings
   555

   557	def looks_like_pickle(data):
   558	    """Best-effort: does a complete pickle stream parse at offset 0?"""
   559	    if not data:
   560	        return False
   561	    try:
   562	        for op, arg, off in pickletools.genops(data):
   563	            if op.name == "STOP":
   564	                return True
   565	            if off > 4_000_000:
   566	                return False
   567	    except Exception:
   568	        return False
   569	    return False

     1	"""Non-executing pickle analysis.
     2	
     3	The scanner must never run the artifact, so it cannot call ``pickle.load``.
     4	Instead it walks the opcode stream with ``pickletools.genops`` and runs a
     5	symbolic machine that mirrors CPython's unpickler stack: it tracks what each
     6	stack entry *is* (a global reference, a module, a ``functools.partial``, a
     7	constant, ...) without importing or calling anything.  A finding is raised at
     8	the opcode that would actually invoke a capability-bearing callable -- REDUCE,
     9	an argument-bearing INST/OBJ, or a retargeted partial reached through the memo,
    10	``getattr``, ``attrgetter``, ``methodcaller`` or a nested stream -- which is
    11	exactly the policy's test (see ``/app/docs/threat-model.md`` section 3).
    12	"""

    15	import pickletools

    17	from modelgate import policy

    20	# Tunable guards so a hostile or pathological artifact cannot exhaust time or
    21	# stack.  Pickles in real models are tiny; these ceilings are far above them.
    22	_MAX_OPS = 2_000_000

    24	
    25	_MARK = object()

    28	# Symbolic values are small sequences tagged by their first element:
    29	#   ("global", module, name)      a GLOBAL / STACK_GLOBAL / INST class
    30	#   ("module", name)              a module object (from __import__/import_module)
    31	#   ("instance", module, name)    an object constructed from that class, so a
    32	#                                 later method call can be resolved on it
    33	#   ["partial", func, [args]]     a functools.partial -- a *list*, so a BUILD
    34	#                                 retarget is seen through the memo and stack
    35	#   ("attrgetter", [names])       operator.attrgetter(...)
    36	#   ("methodcaller", name, [args])operator.methodcaller(...)
    37	#   ("const", value)              a str/bytes/int/float/bool/None literal
    38	#   ("tuple", [items])            a tuple
    39	#   ("list", [items])             a list (contents tracked best-effort)
    40	#   ("opaque",)                   anything whose identity does not matter
    41	_OPAQUE = ("opaque",)

    44	def _const_str(sym):
    45	    if sym and sym[0] == "const" and isinstance(sym[1], str):
    46	        return sym[1]

    50	def _const_bytes(sym):

    56	# Pure data transforms an attacker may wrap embedded loader input in.  Each
    57	# maps a constant to a constant; applying them unpacks bytes (like the archive
    58	# layer) and never runs artifact code.
    59	_TRANSFORMS = {
    60	    "zlib.decompress", "gzip.decompress", "bz2.decompress", "lzma.decompress",
    61	    "base64.b64decode", "base64.standard_b64decode", "base64.urlsafe_b64decode",
    62	    "base64.b85decode", "base64.b32decode", "base64.b16decode", "base64.a85decode",
    63	    "binascii.a2b_base64", "binascii.unhexlify", "binascii.a2b_hex",

    69	def _apply_transform(full, args):
    70	    raw = None

    72	        raw = _const_bytes(args[0])

    74	            s = _const_str(args[0])

    76	                raw = s.encode("latin1", "ignore")
    77	    if raw is None or len(raw) > _TRANSFORM_CAP:
    78	        return None
    79	    try:
    80	        mod, fn = full.split(".", 1)
    81	        if full == "zlib.decompress":
    82	            import zlib
    83	            out = zlib.decompress(raw)
    84	        elif full == "gzip.decompress":
    85	            import gzip
    86	            out = gzip.decompress(raw)
    87	        elif full == "bz2.decompress":
    88	            import bz2
    89	            out = bz2.decompress(raw)
    90	        elif full == "lzma.decompress":
    91	            import lzma
    92	            out = lzma.decompress(raw)
    93	        elif mod == "base64":
    94	            import base64
    95	            out = getattr(base64, fn)(raw)
    96	        elif mod == "binascii":
    97	            import binascii
    98	            out = getattr(binascii, fn)(raw)

   114	class _Machine:
   115	    def __init__(self, data, location, stream, sink, depth, budget):
   116	        self.data = data
   117	        self.location = location
   118	        self.stream = stream
   119	        self.sink = sink            # list to append Findings to
   120	        self.depth = depth
   121	        self.budget = budget        # dict with an "ops" counter
   122	        self.stack = []
   123	        self.memo = {}
   124	
   125	    # -- stack helpers -----------------------------------------------------
   126	    def _pop(self):
   127	        return self.stack.pop() if self.stack else _OPAQUE
   128	
   129	    def _pop_mark(self):
   130	        items = []
   131	        while self.stack:
   132	            top = self.stack.pop()
   133	            if top is _MARK:
   134	                break
   135	            items.append(top)
   136	        items.reverse()
   137	        return items

   139	    def _finding(self, kind, pos, detail):
   140	        where = f"{self.location}#s{self.stream}@{pos}"
   141	        self.sink.append(Finding(kind, where, detail))

   143	    # -- run ---------------------------------------------------------------
   144	    def run(self, gen, base):
   145	        """Drive the opcode generator, rebasing offsets onto ``base``.  Returns
   146	        the STOP offset (relative to base) or None.  Consumes lazily and stops
   147	        at the op budget so a huge pickle is never fully materialised."""
   148	        for op, arg, off in gen:
   149	            self.budget["ops"] += 1
   150	            if self.budget["ops"] > _MAX_OPS:
   151	                return None
   152	            name = op.name
   153	            if name == "STOP":
   154	                return off
   155	            handler = _HANDLERS.get(name)
   156	            if handler is not None:
   157	                handler(self, arg, base + off)
   158	            # opcodes without a handler have no effect we care about
   159	        return None

   161	    # -- the one interesting operation: a call --------------------------
   162	    def invoke(self, func, args, pos):
   163	        """Model calling ``func(*args)`` and return the symbolic result.
   164	
   165	        Raises findings into the sink as a side effect.  ``args`` is a list of
   166	        symbolic values.
   167	        """
   168	        tag = func[0] if func else "opaque"
   169	
   170	        if tag == "partial":
   171	            return self.invoke(func[1], list(func[2]) + list(args), pos)
   172	
   173	        if tag == "attrgetter":
   174	            # Retrieving an attribute is not itself a call; it yields the
   175	            # attribute so a later call can reach it.
   176	            if func[1] and args:
   177	                return self._attr_of(args[0], func[1][0])

   179	
   180	        if tag == "methodcaller":
   181	            if args:
   182	                target = self._attr_of(args[0], func[1])
   183	                if target[0] == "global":
   184	                    return self.invoke(target, func[2], pos)
   185	            return _OPAQUE
   186	
   187	        if tag != "global":
   188	            return _OPAQUE
   189	
   190	        module, name = policy.resolve(func[1], func[2])
   191	        full = f"{module}.{name}"
   192	
   193	        if full in _TRANSFORMS:
   194	            # A pure data transform (decompress/decode): compute it on the
   195	            # constant so a nested loader fed the *result* is seen through.
   196	            # This runs no artifact code -- it only unpacks bytes, as the
   197	            # container layer already does -- and is capped against bombs.
   198	            out = _apply_transform(full, args)
   199	            return ("const", out) if out is not None else _OPAQUE
   200	
   201	        kind = policy.INDIRECTION.get(full)
   202	        if kind is not None:
   203	            return self._indirect(kind, args, pos)
   204	
   205	        fmt = policy.NESTED_LOADERS.get(full)
   206	        if fmt is not None:
   207	            self._nested(fmt, full, args, pos)
   208	            return _OPAQUE
   209	
   210	        cap = policy.CAPABILITIES.get(full)
   211	        if cap is not None:
   212	            kind, trigger = cap
   213	            if trigger == "call" or (trigger == "call_args" and len(args) >= 1):
   214	                self._finding(kind, pos, f"call {full}")

   216	
   217	        # Not a capability: calling a class yields an instance of it, so a
   218	        # later method call (via getattr/methodcaller) can be resolved.
   219	        return ("instance", module, name)
   220	
   221	    def _attr_of(self, obj, attr):

   223	            return _OPAQUE
   224	        if obj[0] == "module":
   225	            return ("global", obj[1], attr)
   226	        if obj[0] in ("global", "instance"):

   230	    def _indirect(self, kind, args, pos):
   231	        if kind == "getattr":

   233	                attr = _const_str(args[1])
   234	                if attr is not None:
   235	                    return self._attr_of(args[0], attr)

   237	        if kind == "import":
   238	            if args:
   239	                mod = _const_str(args[0])

   241	                    return ("module", mod)

   243	        if kind == "attrgetter":

   253	            if args:
   254	                return ["partial", args[0], list(args[1:])]

   523	    """Scan one file that is a sequence of one or more concatenated pickles.
   524

   526	    policy notes); trailing non-pickle bytes -- the raw storages of a legacy
   527	    torch checkpoint -- end the walk once at least one stream has parsed.

   530	        budget = {"ops": 0}

   532	    pos = 0
   533	    stream = 0
   534	    n = len(data)
   535	    parsed_any = False
   536	    while pos < n and budget["ops"] <= _MAX_OPS:
   537	        stream += 1

   543	            # pickle (a legacy torch checkpoint's storages) end the walk; a
   544	            # first stream that will not parse at all is fail-closed.
   545	            if parsed_any or findings:

   522	def scan_pickle(data, location, depth=0, budget=None):
   523	    """Scan one file that is a sequence of one or more concatenated pickles.
   524	
   525	    Every stream is analysed (a payload may hide in the second stream, as the
   526	    policy notes); trailing non-pickle bytes -- the raw storages of a legacy
   527	    torch checkpoint -- end the walk once at least one stream has parsed.
   528	    """
   529	    if budget is None:
   530	        budget = {"ops": 0}
   531	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   532	    pos = 0
   533	    stream = 0
   534	    n = len(data)
   535	    parsed_any = False
   536	    while pos < n and budget["ops"] <= _MAX_OPS:
   537	        stream += 1
   538	        machine = _Machine(data, location, stream, findings, depth, budget)
   539	        try:
   540	            stop_off = machine.run(pickletools.genops(data[pos:]), pos)
   541	        except Exception:
   542	            # A stream that will not parse: trailing raw bytes after an earlier
   543	            # pickle (a legacy torch checkpoint's storages) end the walk; a
   544	            # first stream that will not parse at all is fail-closed.
   545	            if parsed_any or findings:
   546	                break
   547	            return [Finding("unsupported", location, "could not parse pickle opcodes")]
   548	        parsed_any = True
   549	        if stop_off is None:
   550	            break                   # no STOP: truncated tail or op budget hit
   551	        pos += stop_off + 1
   552	    if not parsed_any:
   553	        return [Finding("unsupported", location, "empty pickle")]
   554	    return findings

   558	    """Best-effort: does a complete pickle stream parse at offset 0?"""
   559	    if not data:

   563	            if op.name == "STOP":
   564	                return True
   565	            if off > 4_000_000:

     7	constant, ...) without importing or calling anything.  A finding is raised at

   526	    policy notes); trailing non-pickle bytes -- the raw storages of a legacy
   527	    torch checkpoint -- end the walk once at least one stream has parsed.
   528	    """
   529	    if budget is None:

   565	            if off > 4_000_000:

1	"""Format detection and container recursion.
     2	
     3	Content, not extension, decides the format at every level (threat model
     4	section 2).  ``scan_bytes`` sniffs a magic, routes to the right analyser, and
     5	for compressed or archived artifacts unpacks in memory -- never to disk -- and
     6	recurses on each member by that member's own format, up to the nesting the
     7	policy allows.  Nothing here loads or runs an artifact; archives are read with
     8	``zipfile``/``tarfile`` and decompressors with a hard output cap so a bomb
     9	cannot exhaust memory or time.
    10	"""

    12	
    13	import ast
    14	import io
    15	import struct
    16	import tarfile
    17	import zipfile
    18	
    19	import posixpath
    20	
    21	from modelgate import keras_scan, pickle_scan, savedmodel_scan
    22	from modelgate.report import Finding
    23	
    24	_MAX_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024      # cap on any single decompressed/read blob
    25	_MAX_DEPTH = 6                      # policy nests to 3; a margin, then stop
    26	_MAX_MEMBERS = 4096
    27	_TOTAL_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024   # cumulative read cap per artifact
    28	
    29	
    30	def _over_budget(budget):
    31	    return budget.get("bytes", 0) > _TOTAL_BYTES
    32	
    33	
    34	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    35	def detect(data):
    36	    if data[:2] == b"\x1f\x8b":
    37	        return "gzip"
    38	    if data[:3] == b"BZh":
    39	        return "bz2"
    40	    if data[:6] == b"\xfd7zXZ\x00":
    41	        return "xz"
    42	    if data[:4] in (b"PK\x03\x04", b"PK\x05\x06", b"PK\x07\x08") or _is_zip(data):
    43	        return "zip"
    44	    if data[:8] == b"\x89HDF\r\n\x1a\n":
    45	        return "hdf5"
    46	    if data[:6] == b"\x93NUMPY":
    47	        return "npy"
    48	    if len(data) >= 262 and data[257:262] == b"ustar":
    49	        return "tar"
    50	    if pickle_scan.looks_like_pickle(data):
    51	        return "pickle"
    52	    if _is_tar(data):
    53	        return "tar"
    54	    return "unknown"
    55	
    56	
    57	def _is_zip(data):
    58	    try:
    59	        return zipfile.is_zipfile(io.BytesIO(data))
    60	    except Exception:
    61	        return False
    62	
    63	
    64	def _is_tar(data):
    65	    try:
    66	        with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data)) as tf:
    67	            return tf.next() is not None
    68	    except Exception:
    69	        return False
    70	
    71	
    72	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    73	def scan_bytes(data, location, depth=0, budget=None):
    74	    if budget is None:
    75	        budget = {"ops": 0}
    76	    if depth > _MAX_DEPTH:
    77	        return []
    78	    fmt = detect(data)
    79	    try:
    80	        if fmt in ("gzip", "bz2", "xz"):
    81	            out = _decompress(data, fmt)
    82	            budget["bytes"] = budget.get("bytes", 0) + len(out)
    83	            return scan_bytes(out, f"{location}!{fmt}", depth + 1, budget)
    84	        if fmt == "zip":
    85	            return _scan_zip(data, location, depth, budget)
    86	        if fmt == "tar":
    87	            return _scan_tar(data, location, depth, budget)
    88	        if fmt == "hdf5":
    89	            return keras_scan.scan_h5_bytes(data, location)
    90	        if fmt == "npy":
    91	            return scan_npy_bytes(data, location, depth, budget)
    92	        if fmt == "pickle":
    93	            return pickle_scan.scan_pickle(data, location, depth, budget)
    94	    except Exception as exc:
    95	        # A member that declares a real format but will not parse is treated
    96	        # fail-closed; an unrecognised blob at the top level likewise.
    97	        return [Finding("unsupported", location, f"could not analyse {fmt}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")]
    98	    # Unknown content: at the top level the policy is fail-closed; inside an
    99	    # archive it is just a non-model file (a README, a text card) -> clean.
   100	    if depth == 0:
   101	        return [Finding("unsupported", location, "unrecognised artifact format")]
   102	    return []
   103	
   104	
   105	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   106	def _decompress(data, kind):
   107	    if kind == "gzip":
   108	        import gzip
   109	        reader = gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data))
   110	    elif kind == "bz2":
   111	        import bz2
   112	        reader = bz2.BZ2File(io.BytesIO(data))
   113	    else:
   114	        import lzma
   115	        reader = lzma.LZMAFile(io.BytesIO(data))
   116	    with reader:
   117	        out = reader.read(_MAX_BYTES + 1)
   118	    if len(out) > _MAX_BYTES:
   119	        raise ValueError("decompressed output exceeds cap")
   120	    return out
   121	
   122	
   123	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   124	def _effective_members(zf):
   125	    """Last entry with a given name wins, as zipfile's own lookup does."""
   126	    effective = {}
   127	    for info in zf.infolist():
   128	        effective[info.filename] = info
   129	    return effective
   130	
   131	
   132	def _scan_zip(data, location, depth, budget):
   133	    findings = []
   134	    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf:
   135	        members = _effective_members(zf)
   136	        names = list(members)
   137	        is_torch = any(n == "data.pkl" or n.endswith("/data.pkl") for n in names)
   138	        is_keras = "config.json" in names and "metadata.json" in names
   139	        npy_names = [n for n in names if n.endswith(".npy")]
   140	        is_npz = bool(npy_names) and all(
   141	            n.endswith(".npy") or n.endswith("/") for n in names
   142	        )
   143	        if is_torch:
   144	            for n in names:
   145	                if n == "data.pkl" or n.endswith("/data.pkl"):
   146	                    findings.extend(pickle_scan.scan_pickle(
   147	                        _read_member(zf, members[n], budget), f"{location}!{n}", depth + 1, budget))
   148	            return findings
   149	        if is_keras:
   150	            raw = _read_member(zf, members["config.json"], budget)
   151	            return keras_scan.scan_model_json(raw, f"{location}!config.json")
   152	        if is_npz:
   153	            for n in npy_names:
   154	                if _over_budget(budget):
   155	                    break
   156	                findings.extend(scan_npy_bytes(
   157	                    _read_member(zf, members[n], budget), f"{location}!{n}", depth + 1, budget))
   158	            return findings
   159	        # Generic archive: load each member by its own format.
   160	        count = 0
   161	        for n, info in members.items():
   162	            if n.endswith("/") or getattr(info, "is_dir", lambda: False)():
   163	                continue
   164	            count += 1
   165	            if count > _MAX_MEMBERS or _over_budget(budget):
   166	                break
   167	            findings.extend(_scan_member(
   168	                _read_member(zf, info, budget), n, f"{location}!{n}", depth + 1, budget))
   169	    return findings
   170	
   171	
   172	def _scan_member(data, name, location, depth, budget):
   173	    """Scan one archive member, routing by name where the member is part of a
   174	    multi-file format (a SavedModel's protobuf, a .keras config) and otherwise
   175	    by content."""
   176	    base = posixpath.basename(name)
   177	    try:
   178	        if base == "saved_model.pb":
   179	            return savedmodel_scan.scan_saved_model_bytes(data, location, text=False)
   180	        if base == "saved_model.pbtxt":
   181	            return savedmodel_scan.scan_saved_model_bytes(data, location, text=True)
   182	        if base == "config.json":
   183	            return keras_scan.scan_model_json(data, location)
   184	    except Exception as exc:
   185	        return [Finding("unsupported", location, f"could not analyse member: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")]
   186	    return scan_bytes(data, location, depth, budget)
   187	
   188	
   189	def _read_member(zf, info, budget):
   190	    if info.file_size > _MAX_BYTES:
   191	        raise ValueError("zip member exceeds cap")
   192	    with zf.open(info) as fh:
   193	        blob = fh.read(_MAX_BYTES + 1)
   194	    budget["bytes"] = budget.get("bytes", 0) + len(blob)
   195	    return blob
   196	
   197	
   198	def _scan_tar(data, location, depth, budget):
   199	    findings = []
   200	    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data)) as tf:
   201	        count = 0
   202	        for member in tf:
   203	            if not member.isfile():
   204	                continue
   205	            count += 1
   206	            if count > _MAX_MEMBERS or _over_budget(budget):
   207	                break
   208	            if member.size > _MAX_BYTES:
   209	                continue
   210	            extracted = tf.extractfile(member)
   211	            if extracted is None:
   212	                continue
   213	            blob = extracted.read(_MAX_BYTES + 1)
   214	            budget["bytes"] = budget.get("bytes", 0) + len(blob)
   215	            findings.extend(_scan_member(
   216	                blob, member.name, f"{location}!{member.name}", depth + 1, budget))
   217	    return findings
   218

   221	def scan_npy_bytes(data, location, depth=0, budget=None):
   222	    """A .npy with an object dtype carries a pickle after its header; any other
   223	    dtype is raw numbers and loads nothing."""
   224	    if budget is None:
   225	        budget = {"ops": 0}
   226	    if data[:6] != b"\x93NUMPY":
   227	        return [Finding("unsupported", location, "not a .npy file")]
   228	    major = data[6]
   229	    if major == 1:
   230	        hlen = struct.unpack("<H", data[8:10])[0]
   231	        start = 10 + hlen
   232	    else:
   233	        hlen = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]
   234	        start = 12 + hlen
   235	    header = data[(10 if major == 1 else 12):start].decode("latin1")
   236	    if not _is_object_dtype(header):
   237	        return []
   238	    return pickle_scan.scan_pickle(data[start:], f"{location}:npy-data", depth, budget)
   239	
   240	
   241	def _is_object_dtype(header):
   242	    try:
   243	        meta = ast.literal_eval(header.strip())
   244	        descr = meta.get("descr")
   245	    except Exception:
   246	        return "'|O'" in header or '"|O"' in header or "O8" in header
   247	    return _descr_has_object(descr)
   248	
   249	
   250	def _descr_has_object(descr):
   251	    if isinstance(descr, str):
   252	        return "O" in descr
   253	    if isinstance(descr, (list, tuple)):
   254	        return any(_descr_has_object(item) for item in descr)
   255	    return False
